report:
Brain, right cerebellar tumour

Received in formalin are fragments of soft tumour tissue from the cerebellum, measuring 45 x 35 x 20 mm in aggregate. The cut surface is soft and grey-tan with areas of haemorrhage and yellow necrosis. Representative sections are taken; see block key.

(A1-A6) tumour.

Specimen
- Procedure: Suboccipital craniectomy and excision
- Tumour site: Right cerebellum
- Extent of resection as stated by the surgeon: Gross total resection
- Specimen integrity: Fragmented, received in pieces

Microscopic findings
- Tumour histology:
  Sections show a biphasic glial neoplasm in which compact piloid areas
  containing Rosenthal fibres alternate with loose microcystic areas containing
  eosinophilic granular bodies. The tumour shows a biphasic pattern with
  Rosenthal fibres and eosinophilic granular bodies. Mitoses are not identified
  in 10 high-power fields. On immunohistochemistry, the tumour cells are
  positive for GFAP and OLIG2. The Ki-67 proliferation index is approximately
  2 per cent. On molecular testing, IDH1 R132H is not expressed and a
  KIAA1549-BRAF fusion is detected.
- Treatment effect: No known presurgical therapy

Integrated diagnosis
- Integrated diagnosis: Pilocytic astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 1
- Histopathological classification: Pilocytic astrocytoma
- CNS WHO grade: 1

Molecular information
- IDH1 R132H (immunohistochemistry): Negative
- Other molecular studies: A KIAA1549-BRAF fusion is detected

Additional findings
- None identified

BRAIN, right cerebellum, suboccipital craniectomy and excision
- PILOCYTIC ASTROCYTOMA, CNS WHO grade 1; see synoptic report
